title: Commercial Overview
oneLine: Shows the whole commercial desk at a glance so you can decide what to work on next.
steps: Open Commercial from the sidebar — Overview is the first row; give the figures a moment to arrive.
Read the tiles across the top: open enquiries, open orders, active holds, awaiting dispatch check, advance still short.
Click a tile that is a link to open the list it counts.
For holds and the advance tile, click the small grey i instead — the working links sit inside that panel.
Click any stage box under Orders by stage to open the orders board already filtered to that stage.
Click a lapsing hold's reference to open that order's stock tab, where holds are extended or released.
Scan Latest activity for the last twelve things that happened, then do the work on the screen you land on.

refusals.what: Nothing here can be edited or saved
refusals.why: It is a reading screen only — every figure is a doorway into the list it counts, and the work happens there.

refusals.what: Goods cannot leave while the advance is short
refusals.why: Goods do not leave the yard before the agreed share of the money has arrived; it is an amount, not a tick.

refusals.what: Only Santosh or the admin may waive an advance
refusals.why: Letting a truck go without the money is a commercial decision the manager owns in writing; the reason is required and recorded.

refusals.what: The bay 5 team cannot open this screen
refusals.why: Their whole job is verifying packed slabs, so they were given that one screen and none of the desk's figures to read.

gotchas: The numbers freeze when the page opens — nothing refreshes itself, so reload before quoting any figure in a meeting.
A lapse time already in the past means the hold is gone, not going; opening it settles the record.
Lapsing holds stop counting at twenty, so read twenty as twenty-or-more and work the list down.

deskNotes.santosh: Sees every tile except the two production-planning ones, and is the only person who can waive an advance, in writing.
deskNotes.setumani: Her advance panel tells her to record the money and never offers the waiver; she can open enquiries but only read them.
deskNotes.raghav: No enquiry count, holds, lapsing-holds card or advance tile at all; his dispatch tile opens Packing Lists.
deskNotes.murali: Can read the holds and the lapsing list but not extend or release them; his dispatch tile opens Packing Lists; no waiver.
deskNotes.bay5: No Overview at all — they reach the dispatch check from Verification in their own sidebar.

handsTo: Nothing moves from here; the Overview hands the reader to the order, list or card they clicked.

title: Logging and converting enquiries
oneLine: Write down every customer request before there is an order, then turn the real ones into orders.
steps: Open Enquiries; it lands on Open (New plus Quoted). Press Search or Enter to filter — typing alone does nothing.
Press "Log an enquiry", then pick the customer from the master, or type a prospect name if they are new.
Fill contact name, e-mail and phone; set the date, how it arrived, the subject, and what they said.
Add one line per item — our design or the customer's SKU on each; blank rows are thrown away.
Leave the number box blank so the next number is issued, then save; the enquiry opens on its own page.
Edit and Save enquiry as answers come in; attach the real customer here once they are on the master.
Mark quoted when the quote goes out; to convert, check the order kind, then press Create the order.

refusals.what: Saving with no customer and no prospect name
refusals.why: An enquiry from nobody cannot be followed up — there has to be someone to answer.

refusals.what: Creating the order before a customer is saved on the enquiry
refusals.why: The invoice, packing list and challan all take the party details from the customer's record; a prospect has none. Picking one is not enough — save first.

refusals.what: Marking an enquiry lost without typing a reason
refusals.why: Price, lead time, went to another supplier — it is the question asked months later, and nobody remembers it.

refusals.what: A line with neither our design nor the customer's SKU
refusals.why: A line naming neither describes nothing. Nothing on the form saves until it is fixed, so a half-typed table never half-lands.

gotchas: Create the order is instant and one-way — no confirmation, no undo. It issues the order number and marks the enquiry Ordered.
Order kind is guessed from the customer's country text; only "India" pre-picks Domestic. Check the dropdown before converting.
Editing lines after conversion changes nothing on the order — it took its own copy. Correct them on the order screen.

deskNotes.setumani: Read-only here. The "Log an enquiry" button still looks live but turns her away — Santosh or Murali logs it.
deskNotes.raghav: No access to enquiries at all; he picks the work up at the checklist, the invoice and the challan.
deskNotes.bay5: No access — dispatch has one screen only.

handsTo: Convert makes a draft order with the lines and the customer's terms; Setumani prices it and raises the PI.

title: Customers (the client master)
oneLine: The one record of who a customer is and what prints on their paperwork.
steps: Open Clients from the sidebar and search by name, e-mail or customer code - nothing else is matched.
Check they are not already on the master, inactive ones included; International Sales adds customers here too.
Press New customer and save with at least a name; a duplicate name is allowed, so check first.
Open the customer and fill their code, contact, e-mail, phone, address, city, country and two-digit state code.
Fill GSTIN, PAN, currency, incoterm, delivery and payment terms and port of discharge - orders copy these.
Fill the printed Bill to, Ship to and Notify party blocks; the first line is the party's name.
Press Save customer - it writes every box, empty ones included, and there is no undo afterwards.

refusals.what: Saving a customer with no name.
refusals.why: The name is what prints as the party block on the invoice and proforma; a blank one would go out on paper.

refusals.what: A GSTIN or PAN in the wrong shape.
refusals.why: It stops a phone number or half-pasted string being filed as a GSTIN. Shape only, so still read it back against their paperwork.

refusals.what: A state code that is not exactly two digits.
refusals.why: Two digits is what a GST state code is; it prints on the invoice and says which state the buyer sits in.

refusals.what: Deleting a customer - there is no Delete.
refusals.why: Every past invoice, proforma and packing list points back at this row, and International Sales shares it. Mark them inactive instead.

gotchas: An order copies the tax and address details when the customer is picked; correcting them here later won't fix documents already raised.
Country decides everything: India means a domestic order that carries GST, and a blank country counts as export.
Marking inactive saves instantly with no confirmation and removes them from everyone's pick lists; the same button puts them back.

deskNotes.setumani: You can open and read every field but not type or save; ask Santosh or Murali to make the change.
deskNotes.raghav: Read only, and the enquiry numbers on a customer's page will not open for you - use the order links instead.
deskNotes.murali: You add and edit here like Santosh; your challans pull the consignee name, address and GSTIN off these rows, so keep them right.
deskNotes.bay5: Not your screen - you are sent back to Dispatch Check if you land on it.

handsTo: Enquiries - Murali or Santosh raise one against this customer; the order copies these details onto Parties.

title: The order page
oneLine: The one page that holds a customer's whole deal: terms, lines, money and the checklist.
steps: Pick Export or Domestic, then the client — the client's terms and addresses fill themselves in.
Create the order, then add the lines on the Items tab; each line needs a design, description or SKU.
Check the order total — the advance is a percentage of it, so unpriced lines stop dispatch.
Hold the slabs on the Stock tab; that is what lets the proforma go out.
Record each payment on the Receipts card as it arrives, dated the day it landed.
Work the 22-point checklist, mark it checked, then ask the manager to approve it.
Tick the order tasks — booking, CHA, BL, COO, e-way bill — as each is done.

refusals.what: No proforma until the slabs are held
refusals.why: A proforma promises specific slabs, so those slabs must be held against the order before the customer is given the promise.

refusals.what: No final invoice until the checklist is approved
refusals.why: Two signatures, two people: Commercial prepares and checks the sheet, the manager approves it, and the invoice waits on that approval.

refusals.what: The truck does not leave before the advance
refusals.why: Packing and loading may run ahead of the money; dispatch may not. Unpriced lines stop it too: no total, no advance.

refusals.what: Only the manager cancels, waives or lowers the advance
refusals.why: Each one undoes money promised or kills a numbered document the customer has seen, so it costs a name and a written reason.

gotchas: Delete on a line is instant, no warning, and renumbers the rest — line 4 becomes line 3 on every later document.
Closing sweeps every slab still reserved into dispatched, and a closed order can never move, take money, or be changed.
Changing the client on a saved order overwrites the addresses and terms — re-check anything you had typed by hand.

deskNotes.santosh: Yours alone: cancel an order, approve the checklist, waive or lower the advance, delete a receipt.
deskNotes.setumani: Write anything here — orders, lines, terms, receipts, checklist — but record the money only; waiving and approving are the manager's.
deskNotes.raghav: Read any order, but only the checklist points, the order tasks and the Invoice tab are yours to fill. Save, Add line and Record receipt look live and will be refused.
deskNotes.murali: Create and edit orders in full, and delete a receipt. Your Approve button on the checklist looks live but is always refused — never plan around it.
deskNotes.bay5: You never work here; typing this address sends you straight back to the Dispatch Check.

handsTo: Hold the slabs on the Stock tab next — Setumani or Santosh — then the proforma follows.

title: Stock check and holds
oneLine: Find out whether the slabs are standing in the yard, then reserve them for this order.
steps: Open the order's Stock tab and press Check stock on a line — it needs a design name first.
Read the result — slabs group by batch — and narrow by thickness or exact grade if needed.
Tick the slabs; the batch header ticks a whole batch, and the counter shows picked against needed.
Leave Days at the standard unless you have a reason; the reference is fixed to this order.
Press Place hold — the order moves to Stock checked, logged under your name.
To give slabs back, open Slabs on the hold, tick them, add a reason, release.
If stock was short, ask an admin to raise the production request for the shortfall.

refusals.what: Holding a slab already held or packed
refusals.why: Somebody got there first. Two orders can never both be promised the same stone.

refusals.what: Holding a cut slab, or one whose mark can't be read
refusals.why: A cut-to-size slab is refused at dispatch, so counting it here only promises the customer something the lorry cannot carry.

refusals.what: Releasing a hold that has lapsed or been packed
refusals.why: A spent hold is history — usually the days ran out while the page sat open. Refresh and place a new one.

refusals.what: Raising the production request yourself
refusals.why: The plant's queue was kept with the admin login, so all four commercial desks are refused today. Ask an admin.

gotchas: No Extend button: when the days run out the slabs go back, the order drops to Confirmed, and the PI blocks again.
Trust the countdown, not the green active chip — a lapsed hold still offers Release buttons that then refuse.
Days outside 1–60 is silently ignored and the standard used — check the expiry on the hold card.

deskNotes.murali: May search stock and read every hold, but cannot place or release one — the buttons look live and refuse when pressed.
deskNotes.raghav: Stock search refuses him entirely, so no slabs to tick; he can only read the holds and production requests already on the order.
deskNotes.bay5: Never opens an order screen, so never sees this — held slabs reach you through the packing list.

handsTo: The hold unlocks the proforma invoice; Setumani or Santosh raises the PI on the next tab.

title: The order checklist
oneLine: The 22 questions about an order that must be answered before the proforma, and signed off before invoicing.
steps: Open the order and scroll down its Overview tab — the checklist card sits below the receipts.
Fill the cards above it first and press Save header; the checklist fills itself in from those answers.
Work the 22 rows: type any missing answers, tick Settled, then press Save answers.
Chase the sender for whatever the sheet still calls outstanding, before the proforma goes out.
Press Mark checked to stamp yourself as preparer; the manager then presses Approve.
Work the task list below: tick each done line, set its date; notes save when you click away.
Press Not required to retire a line — nothing here can be deleted. Add extras at the bottom.

refusals.what: Final invoice before the checklist is approved
refusals.why: The invoice is what the customer and bank act on, so a second person confirms the terms first. A draft may be prepared meanwhile.

refusals.what: Approving, unless you are the manager or an admin
refusals.why: The sheet carries two signatures on purpose — whoever prepares it cannot also be the one who signs it off.

refusals.what: Dating a task line you have not ticked
refusals.why: A completion date on unfinished work is the one thing on that card anyone would later read as fact.

refusals.what: Adding a task already on the list
refusals.why: Two lines with the same name means two people ticking different copies of the same job.

gotchas: Mark checked does not save your typing — press Save answers first, or unsaved boxes are wiped.
Clearing a box the system filled just refills it; change the answer in the cards above instead.
You can approve with points still open — the outstanding count is the only warning you get.

deskNotes.santosh: Approve is yours alone, as is Cancel order — cancelling closes the order permanently and releases everything held against it.
deskNotes.raghav: You fill the sheet but cannot change the cards above it; ask Santosh or Setumani to correct answers fed from there. Work the tasks from the Documents tab.
deskNotes.murali: Your Approve button looks live but the press is refused — approval is Santosh's. Raise it rather than work around it.
deskNotes.bay5: You never reach this screen; your part is the Dispatch Check.

handsTo: Once Santosh approves, the final invoice is unblocked for Setumani or Raghav; the task list keeps running.

title: Proforma invoice (PI)
oneLine: The priced offer the customer pays against — numbered, frozen when issued, and never edited afterwards.
steps: Open the order's Proforma tab; fix any amber warning about missing items or consignee on the order first.
Press Create draft from this order — parties, lines, quantities and rates freeze onto a brand-new proforma number.
Edit the draft to add bank account, GST registration, delivery date, discount, weights, salesperson and terms — prices aren't editable.
Type the Terms and Conditions yourself — the box prints exactly what you type and nothing else.
Open the PDF and check the frozen detail; what you see is exactly what the customer gets.
Make sure a stock hold is live, then press Issue. The order moves to PI issued.
Press Customer accepted when they confirm. If the deal changes later, Revise under a new number.

refusals.what: Issuing without a live stock hold
refusals.why: A PI promises specific material on a date; holds lapse after five days, so a stock-checked order can still be refused.

refusals.what: Editing or re-issuing a PI once it's issued
refusals.why: Once it leaves the building it is the customer's paper; the only way to change it is a fresh numbered document.

refusals.what: Cancelling a PI, or cancelling without a reason
refusals.why: Cancelling destroys a promise the customer may be holding, so it's Santosh's call, and the reason prints beside the struck-through number for ever.

refusals.what: Starting a second revision while one is in draft
refusals.why: Two revisions would burn two numbers and leave two drafts racing to replace one paper the customer already holds.

gotchas: The draft freezes the moment you create it; editing the order afterwards changes nothing — build a fresh draft or revise.
Issuing any draft cancels every other live PI on the order — never build a second draft just to compare.
Revise doesn't retire the old PI until you issue the replacement, and drafts can't be deleted — only cancelled.

deskNotes.santosh: Only he or an admin can cancel a PI, including scrapping a draft nobody wants.
deskNotes.setumani: Builds, edits, issues, revises and records acceptance — but Cancel stays greyed; ask Santosh.
deskNotes.raghav: Read-only here: he can open any PI and its PDF, but never build or issue one.
deskNotes.murali: Read-only too — look at any PI, open the PDF, change nothing.
deskNotes.bay5: Never reaches an order, so this screen never comes up for the dispatch team.

handsTo: Order moves to 'PI issued'. Setumani records the advance receipt; later Raghav's invoice inherits the bank you chose.

title: Packing lists
oneLine: Turns a confirmed order into a real shipment, and moves the stone out of finished goods.
steps: Start from the order's Packing tab: pack a hold, or type slab numbers. One list per order.
Build the crates first with gross and net weight and size in centimetres, then put slabs in them.
Measure every slab and type the real length and width, plus the customer's slab and batch numbers.
For cut-to-size work use the cut-to-size table; crate, drawing and building carry down to the next line.
Fill container, seal, vehicle and weights when booked, then press Save header. That panel does not save itself.
Send for dispatch check. The stone locks to this list that moment; bay 5 then passes or rejects it.
Finalise a passed list, then Mark dispatched when the container leaves; any unfit or unchecked line blocks it.

refusals.what: A second packing list on the same order
refusals.why: One proforma invoice means one shipment; two lists would bill two shipments as one. Reopen a rejected list rather than starting again.

refusals.what: Slabs already packed, held elsewhere, returned, or marked cut-to-size
refusals.why: The container is stuffed from this sheet, so a list claiming stone that is not in the crate is worse than a short list.

refusals.what: Changing crates, slabs or the cm/in switch after sending
refusals.why: Bay 5 is standing at the crates reading that sheet; it must not change under them. Reopen the list first.

refusals.what: Marking dispatched before the advance is recorded
refusals.why: The truck does not leave before the advance. This is the only place money is asked about, so it is deliberately the last check.

gotchas: Sizes arrive pre-filled at 348 x 201, so a slab nobody measured prints a plausible wrong figure on a customs sheet.
A rejected list can be resent without reopening, carrying old passes and refusals. Reopen it first, then rebuild.
Reopening hands every slab back to stock and wipes every verdict, so the floor must check the whole list again.
handsTo: Bay 5 walks the crates and passes or rejects each line; the answer lands back here.

deskNotes.santosh: Only you can waive a short advance, and only with a written reason on the order.
deskNotes.setumani: You build and move the list, but record a short advance on the order; waiving it is Santosh's.
deskNotes.raghav: Read and print only, though every button looks live. Take the finished crates and weights into the invoice.
deskNotes.murali: Read and print only, though every button looks live. Container, seal and weight figures for freight sit here.
deskNotes.bay5: You never open this screen; the list reaches you on your own dispatch check once it is sent.

title: Dispatch check (bay 5)
oneLine: The last look at the crates before stuffing: every line passes, or the whole list goes back.
steps: Tap Refresh, then take the top list off To check - the oldest is holding up a container.
Open it and note which unit the sizes are in: cm on some orders, inches on others.
Work crate by crate, marking every slab and every cut-to-size piece Fit or Unfit.
On Unfit, pick one of the eight reasons or type your own; one tap records it.
On a clean crate use Mark crate as correct - it only touches lines nobody has looked at.
Type a note if Commercial should know something. Optional, and only on a first check.
Tap the big button: green Verify if all fit, red Reject if anything failed.

refusals.what: Can't finish until every line is marked.
refusals.why: A list is verified because every line was looked at, not because somebody scrolled to the bottom of the screen.

refusals.what: An unfit line will not save without a reason.
refusals.why: Unfit sends the list back and pulls the order to Packing. "No reason given" is nothing Commercial can act on at eight at night.

refusals.what: Bulk marking never clears a line already unfit.
refusals.why: It only touches lines nobody has looked at, and always names what it skipped. Losing a real finding is what this screen exists to prevent.

refusals.what: A rejected list takes no further verdicts.
refusals.why: Its findings are already with Commercial; changing them underneath would rewrite the reason it went back. It has to be reopened first.

gotchas: Verify and Reject are one button. It turns red the moment a line is unfit; there is no separate Reject.
Rejecting is one-way from here: unfit slabs go back to stock, and only Commercial can reopen the list.
A verified list still has Fit and Unfit on every line - a crack found during loading stops the truck.
handsTo: Verified: back to Commercial as Ready, then invoice and freight. Rejected: back to Packing for Santosh or Setumani.

deskNotes.bay5: This is your only screen, and it shows no prices, tax numbers or payment terms. You cannot swap a slab or reopen a list.
deskNotes.santosh: Yours and Setumani's alone: reopen a rejected list, and swap a refused slab for one of the same design and thickness. Reopening wipes every verdict, so it comes back as a whole new check.
deskNotes.setumani: Same as Santosh. Watch for a swapped-in slab: it returns unchecked and the truck waits until bay 5 passes it, even though the list reads Verified.
deskNotes.raghav: You cannot see this screen at all - not even greyed out. Wait for the list to come back verified, then raise the invoice and challan.
deskNotes.murali: You cannot see this screen at all. Freight is yours only once the list has passed and Commercial finalises it.

title: Raising and issuing invoices
oneLine: Finish and issue the customer's invoice — the paper he pays against and the load travels with.
steps: Start from the order, not the register: open the order's Invoice tab and press New invoice.
Check the kind (domestic or export) and the invoice date; leave the number blank to take the next one.
Decide whether the lines come from the order's own prices or from a packing list of what was actually packed.
Confirm the registration, the bank and the exchange rate; that rate decides whether a foreign advance counts as paid.
Press Create draft invoice. A number is taken and the document freezes — later order changes do not follow it.
On the draft, price any amber lines, fill vehicle, LR and e-way details, and save each card separately.
Open the PDF and read it, then press Issue. The order moves to Invoiced and the invoice locks.

refusals.what: A second invoice on the same order
refusals.why: One order carries one invoice so nobody bills the same load twice; cancel the wrong one with a reason, then raise again.

refusals.what: Issuing before the checklist is approved
refusals.why: Approval is where someone senior confirms the load is what the customer ordered; billing first demands money for goods nobody signed off.

refusals.what: Editing an invoice once it is issued
refusals.why: The customer already holds that paper; changing it here would leave his copy and ours disagreeing. Cancel it and raise another.

refusals.what: Moving the bank off the proforma's account
refusals.why: The proforma already told the customer where to pay; moving it afterwards is how payments get lost, so it takes the manager.

gotchas: Lines drawn from a packing list can carry no rate. An amber line means those slabs will be billed at zero.
Four save buttons on one invoice page, each saving only its own card. One press saves half your typing.
On a domestic invoice the date picks the number's year: dating one 31 March in April takes last year's number.
handsTo: Raghav sends and files the PDF and builds the export set; the truck still waits for the advance.

deskNotes.santosh: Only you or an admin may cancel an invoice, change the bank, or retype the rate after it is issued.
deskNotes.raghav: Fix the registration and bank while it is still a draft — the export documents copy both from this invoice.
deskNotes.murali: You may read invoices, not change them. On the order's Invoice tab the buttons still appear but refuse when pressed — don't fill the form.
deskNotes.bay5: There is no invoice screen for you; typing the address in puts you back on the Dispatch Check.

title: Delivery challans
oneLine: The four-copy paper for goods that move without being sold — samples, display slabs, sister-company material.
steps: Raise it from the order's Invoice tab when there is an order; otherwise press New challan in the book.
Fill the top row: challan date, PO number and date, commodity, lorry number.
Name the consignee: pick a client, or type name, address and GSTIN yourself, one line per printed line.
Fill each line: description, quantity, unit, SQFT, rate, HSN. Leave Amount blank and it works itself out.
Leave the challan number blank unless you are mirroring a number already issued elsewhere.
Press Create draft challan, then fix anything except the number while it is still a draft.
Press Issue challan, then print the four copies and hand the driver the transporter copy.

refusals.what: Creating or issuing a challan with no lines
refusals.why: The challan is the paper saying what left the yard; a page listing nothing proves nothing at a check post.

refusals.what: Saving without a consignee
refusals.why: The transporter and the check post read that one line to know where the goods are going. Picking a client counts.

refusals.what: Editing or issuing an already-issued challan
refusals.why: Copies are with the driver and Central Excise; their paper and our record must match. Cancel and raise a fresh one.

refusals.what: Cancelling without typing a reason
refusals.why: The cancelled number stays in the book forever, and someone reading it in a year must see why the goods never went.

gotchas: The number is used up the moment you create the draft. Abandoning the draft does not give it back.
A draft prints too. Look for the orange DRAFT or red CANCELLED stamp before handing anything to a driver.
Notes are not internal: they print small on all four copies, cancellation reason included. Keep them fit for outsiders.

deskNotes.santosh: Only you or an admin can cancel a challan, draft or issued, and only with a written reason; the others have no Cancel button.
deskNotes.bay5: The challan book is closed to dispatch logins — you land back on Dispatch Check. Ask the commercial desk to raise one.

handsTo: Four copies leave with the lorry; Raghav and Santosh reconcile it later on the order's Invoice tab.

title: Design codes and colours
oneLine: The master list of our designs — code, shade, colour — and each customer's own article codes and barcodes.
steps: Open Design codes and find the design in the Find box, or narrow to unconfirmed shades and missing colours.
Press Seed from stock to pull in designs finished goods knows about that have no row yet.
Type the owner's item code on the row — it saves the moment you click away.
Pick the shade, light medium or dark; that ticks Confirmed for you. Add notes if useful.
Open the row's colour button, type the colour name and the three readings off the sample, save.
For a customer's own codes, open the customer article list, pick the customer, and check their next barcode.
Add or edit articles, generate blank barcodes, then read the label warnings before printing off a packing list.

refusals.what: An item code already used on another design
refusals.why: That code is how the customer's paperwork names the design; two designs under one code makes an export line ambiguous at their end.

refusals.what: A barcode that is already on another article
refusals.why: A reused code scans as the wrong goods, so that customer's barcodes and crate labels stop until somebody settles whose code it is.

refusals.what: Generating a barcode without the customer's own prefix
refusals.why: A generated code has to continue that customer's own series; invented digits are not a barcode and will collide with somebody's real article.

refusals.what: The same customer, design and size added twice
refusals.why: Those three things are the article's identity; a second row means two codes for one thing. Edit the existing row instead.

gotchas: There is no Save button: each box saves the moment you click away. Only the colour window's five fields save together.
Picking a shade silently ticks Confirmed too — try one on for size and it is recorded as confirmed.
Saving a shade or colour re-times the plant's cleaning hours; the green line afterwards is the only sight you get.
handsTo: The plant's cleaning schedule, Raghav's export documents, and the labels bay 5 sticks on crates and pieces.

deskNotes.setumani: Read and search both screens and print labels, but cannot change any code, shade, colour or barcode.
deskNotes.murali: Same as Setumani — look up anything, print labels, change nothing.
deskNotes.raghav: No access at all; the page is not on his sidebar and the address is refused.
deskNotes.bay5: Never opens this — they only stick on the labels printed here.
